title: Consolidate IO schedulers and introduce prefetch hinting for compact KV priming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Over the last 18 months the serving runtime has accreted three overlapping IO/scheduler paths: the legacy slab-adapter scheduler, the microbatch IO strand, and the new cooperative runloop. Each path applies different admission and prefetch semantics which leads to inconsistent KV priming behavior, duplicated timers, and noisy telemetry. Symptoms include: sporadic tail latency spikes when warmup misses occur, KV-cache churn on tenant handoffs, and difficulty reasoning about admission backpressure for microbatching.

Goal: Consolidate the scheduler/IO control plane into a single, minimal scheduler facade and add an explicit prefetch-hint mechanism that allows the admission layer to tag sessions/requests with soft-prefetch guidance. This should reduce duplicated IO work, make KV priming deterministic across batchers, and enable a simpler rollout path for future prefetch policies. The work also includes upgrading our libaio binding to 2.8.x (compat smoothing) and removing a deprecated slab adapter shim to reduce binary size and heap churn.
tasks: Audit current scheduler callsites and produce a mapping doc (who calls which API and with what timing)
Design scheduler facade API: admission.enqueue(session, hint) + scheduler.runloop metrics hooks
Implement facade that delegates to existing executors but normalizes admission and prefetch semantics
Add prefetch-hint metadata to request envelope and extend KV priming code to respect hint priority
Replace slab-adapter instantiation sites and remove shim with backward-compatible adapter for 2 weeks
Upgrade libaio binding to 2.8.x and run compatibility tests on Linux kernel 5.15+ images
Add unit/integration tests that simulate warmup misses and measure priming coverage
Create benchmarking harness to reproduce tail-latency scenario from benchmark-serve-0624
Canary rollout: start on a single Dedicated pool, run 48h smoke & perf gates
Documentation: update runloop design doc and add migration notes for partners
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler facade behaviors, simulation tests that generate mixed small/large sessions to validate prefetch hit-rate, integration tests exercising libaio upgrade on container images used by dedicated. Capture metrics for 100k requests with varying sequence lengths and compare warmup miss rate before/after.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler facade implemented and replaces duplicated timer sources (no more than 1 timer source per executor)
Prefetch-hint respected by KV priming: hit-rate improvement >= 20% for synthetic warmup-miss workload
End-to-end p95 token latency reduced by at least 8% on benchmark-serve-0624 scenario
No regressions in throughput on standard batching workloads (within ±3%)
Libaio binding upgraded and passes kernel compatibility smoke tests
All deprecated slab-adapter symbols removed and build size reduced by >1MB
Canary run completes with <0.1% increased error rate and no customer impact incidents
rollout_plan: QA cluster validation (2 days): run stress + fuzzer against facade enabled
Canary: enable on a single Dedicated pool (24-48h, increased telemetry)
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% of tenant load for Dedicated over 7 days
Monitor metrics: KV priming hit-rate, tail latency p99/p999, error rate, memory consumption
Rollback plan: feature flag off + revert adapter removal PR if canary triggers (>0.5% errors or latency regression)
Post-mortem and audit: collect key metrics and publish to console runtime-1.28 dashboard
perf_targets: KV priming hit-rate improvement: >= 20% on warmup-heavy traces
End-to-end p95 token latency: -8% improvement target
Memory allocation churn during startup reduced by at least 15%
Build artifact size reduced by >1MB after slab-adapter removal
